steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Social stratification: the hierarchical arrangement of people into social strata based on wealth, income, status and power. In the UK, social class is the primary form of stratification.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Social class systems: the NS-SEC (8 classes from higher managerial to never worked) replaced the Registrar General's scale. Weber: class is based on market situation. Marx: class is based on relationship to means of production.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Life chances: class strongly affects health (working-class die 7-9 years earlier), education (middle-class children achieve higher), income (top 10% earn 12x more than bottom 10%), and housing (overcrowding 5x higher in lowest quintile).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The wealth gap: richest 10% hold 44% of total wealth; poorest 50% hold 9%. This gap has widened since the 1980s. Wilkinson and Pickett: more unequal societies have worse outcomes for everyone.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain what social stratification is and how social class affects life chances. | Describe the extent of wealth inequality in the UK and evaluate explanations for it. | Evaluate whether social class is still relevant in modern society.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Stratification divides society into layers based on wealth, power and status. Class dramatically affects life chances: health, education, income, housing. These inequalities persist across generations | Top 10% own 44% of wealth; bottom 50% own 9%. Marxist: capitalism concentrates wealth. Wilkinson and Pickett: inequality harms everyone. Some inequality may incentivise effort, but extreme inequality  | Class still affects health, education, income, housing. Counter: class identities are weakening; social mobility exists. Conclusion: class is less culturally significant but its material impact remain

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Stratification = structured INEQUALITY. Life chances vary dramatically by class. Wealth gap: top 10% = 44%. Bottom 50% = 9%. WIDENING. Wilkinson & Pickett: inequality harms ALL. Class STILL matters for life chances even if class identity is weakening.
